components.css: .ds-btn-foil { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:9px; font-family:'Archivo',sans-serif; font-weight:700; font-size:0.96rem; padding:12px 22px; border-radius:3px; border:1px solid #8a6523; color:#3a2607; background:linear-gradient(177deg,#e4c57e,#b4893a 46%,#8a6523); box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.5) inset,0 10px 22px -14px rgba(58,38,7,0.9); cursor:pointer; transition:transform .18s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1),box-shadow .18s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-btn-foil:hover { transform:translateY(-1px); box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.6) inset,0 16px 26px -14px rgba(58,38,7,0.95); } .ds-btn-foil:active { transform:translateY(1px); }

components.html: Pemeriksaan tunggalForm A

narrative.overview: Every web asset — a domain, a hosting plan, a TLS certificate — is treated as an entry in an official register with a stamped validity period. The interface is a security-printed ledger: ceremony surfaces are drenched in deep oxblood ink; working surfaces sit on a faintly engine-turned celadon security paper. Status is never a pill or a colored dot — it is a drawn seal plus an overprinted stamp. The world refuses the dark SaaS dashboard and the cream-paper serif certificate alike: no blue, no cream, a heavy grotesque instead of a serif. Gravity comes from guilloché, ruled keylines, gold foil, and monospaced record numerals.
keyCharacteristics: Oxblood ink identity on celadon (never cream) security paper.
Generative guilloché rosettes and drawn SVG validity seals.
Status as seal + overprint stamp, color-coded by validity.
Archivo grotesque display with Spline Sans Mono for all record data.
Depth is printed (rules, keylines, one sheet shadow), not floated.

rules.name: The Oxblood-or-Paper Rule
rules.body: A surface is either drenched oxblood (ceremony) or celadon security paper (work). White and cream are never grounds.

rules.name: The Status-is-Stamped Rule
rules.body: Validity is shown as a drawn seal plus an overprinted stamp in its status color — never a filled pill, a solid badge, or a bare colored dot.

rules.name: The Rare-Foil Rule
rules.body: Gold foil marks the single most important action and the seals; scattering it dilutes the metal.

rules.name: The Numerals-are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Every date, day-count, serial, and legend is Spline Sans Mono with tabular-nums. Archivo never sets record data; mono never sets prose.

rules.name: The Printed-Not-Floating Rule
rules.body: Separation comes from rules, keylines, and guilloché. Only a register sheet casts a shadow; stamps, seals, chips, and rows never float.

dos: Do drench ceremony surfaces (masthead, hero, footer) in oxblood #48101d and keep work surfaces on celadon paper #e7ebe3.
Do set every date, day-count, serial, and legend in Spline Sans Mono with tabular-nums.
Do show validity as a drawn seal + an overprint stamp in the status color.
Do draw every icon as inline SVG in one consistent stroke weight.
Do convey depth with ruled keylines, the inset sheet border, and guilloché; keep the paper's engine-turned tint faint enough that text stays legible.
donts: Don't introduce white or cream as a ground, or any blue accent.
Don't fall back to a generic SaaS card grid (icon + heading + text) or render status as a filled pill or colored dot.
Don't reach for a serif to signal 'certificate' — Archivo grotesque is the display voice; the certificate feeling comes from guilloché, seals, foil, and ruled columns.
Don't float elements with drop shadows; only a register sheet lifts off the ground.
Don't scatter gold foil — it marks the primary action and the seals only.
